learning_outcomes.text: Interprets, translates, and prepares technical documentation in a foreign language. Follows subjects with content in English.

syllabus_topics: UNIT 4: MACHINES AND AUTOMOTIVE ENGINEERING IN A GREENER WORLD
teaching_methods: Introductory activities: At the beginning of the course, students will take an online level test ("online test 1").

Seminars: During the different seminars (and through online explanatory videos), the professor will explain the main characteristics of Technical English within the field of mechanical and chemical engineering. Special emphasis will be placed on improving the student's English language proficiency, and they will be provided with the necessary resources to read technical texts and write paragraphs expressing their opinion, as well as to listen and speak about different topics in their discipline.

Problem/exercise solving: Throughout the course, students will complete different activities that include practice of the 4 skills: reading, writing, listening, and speaking. These activities will provide practice on the theoretical or grammatical aspects presented in class.

Personalized attention: Students can ask questions or talk with their professors about course-related issues individually before or after class and via videoconference through Teams. Students will receive a schedule of office hours at the beginning of the course.

Debates: Students will watch videos and read online texts on different aspects of current engineering to upload their contributions to each proposed debate forum: 1 contribution will be written and another will be oral in an individual video. In these contributions, students will express their opinions on the topic, and they will also have to make specific comments on another student's contribution to the debate.

Reading of written / graphic documentation: Throughout the course, students will read different types of technical texts (encyclopedia articles, popular science magazine articles, specialized magazine articles, science and technology sections of newspapers, etc.) related to different engineering topics and will complete the corresponding activities. Some of these activities will address reading comprehension, text genre, specific text format, and relevant grammatical aspects of the technical texts.

assessment_methods.method: Debate forums contributions (1 written, 1 oral video)

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final grade comprises 50% from three online objective tests, 20% from a practical skills test, 20% from two debate forum contributions (one written, one oral), and 10% from class attendance and active participation. To pass, students must score at least 5 in two of the three online tests and participate in at least one debate forum. For the second sitting, the final grade is based on a single online test (70%) and the average of the two debates submitted during the course (30%). Fraudulent activity in any assessment will result in a failing grade for that activity.
